example.question: A line goes from the bottom left to the top right of the page. Is it straight?

misconceptions.cause: Thinks straight means upright or flat.
misconceptions.reveals: The answer no, it is slanting as a wrong option, with a reason that names the idea.
misconceptions.help: Lay a ruler along it: it does not bend.

misconceptions.error: Calls a wobbly freehand line straight.

example.question: Is a wobbly line drawn without a ruler straight?

misconceptions.cause: Has not checked with a ruler.
misconceptions.reveals: The answer yes as a wrong option, with a reason that names the idea.
misconceptions.help: Check with a ruler edge.

misconceptions.error: Calls a zigzag (two straight lines) a curved line.

example.question: A zigzag line: curved or made of straight lines?

misconceptions.cause: Calls any line that is not one straight line curved.
misconceptions.reveals: The answer curved as a wrong option, with a reason that names the idea.
misconceptions.help: Look at each part: each part is straight.

misconceptions.error: Lets the ruler slip so the line bends at the end.

example.question: Your line bends at the end. What happened?

misconceptions.cause: Does not hold the ruler firmly.
misconceptions.reveals: The answer nothing as a wrong option, with a reason that names the idea.
misconceptions.help: Press the ruler down with the other hand.

misconceptions.error: Calls a corner a curve.

example.question: The corner of a book: curved or straight?

misconceptions.cause: Thinks any turn is a curve.
misconceptions.reveals: The answer curved as a wrong option, with a reason that names the idea.
misconceptions.help: A curve bends smoothly; a corner turns sharply.

misconceptions.error: Thinks a circle edge is not a line.

example.question: Is the edge of a plate a curved line?

misconceptions.reveals: The answer no as a wrong option, with a reason that names the idea.
misconceptions.help: Trace the plate edge with a finger.

misconceptions.error: Tries to draw a curved line with a ruler and gets straight pieces.

example.question: How do you draw a rainbow line?

misconceptions.cause: Uses a ruler for all lines.
misconceptions.reveals: The answer with a ruler as a wrong option, with a reason that names the idea.
misconceptions.help: Draw curves freehand or round a round object.

misconceptions.error: Calls a gently wavy line straight.

example.question: A road on a map bends gently. Straight or curved?

misconceptions.reveals: The answer straight as a wrong option, with a reason that names the idea.
misconceptions.help: Lay a ruler on it: does it leave the ruler?

learning_experiences: recognise and name different shapes in the environment (triangles, squares, circles and ovals),
in pairs or groups, discuss types of lines in different shapes (triangles, squares, circles and ovals)
in turns, name different shapes of objects or on surfaces in their classroom,
draw triangles, squares, circles and ovals on manila papers and display in the learning environment,
in groups, make patterns using triangles, squares, circles and ovals, colour them and share with other groups,
play games involving pattern making using digital devices or other resources.
key_inquiry_questions: How can patterns be made using shapes?
sub_strands.design_notes: Outcomes a to c are KICD's words; d is attitudinal. Shapes are triangles, squares, circles and ovals (and rectangles from Grade 1). Drawing shapes is done in class; shape patterns can be asked as 'what comes next'.

source.version: PDF on disk, text layer (read in place)

outcomes.text: identify different shapes in the environment
draw shapes in different ways
draw patterns involving different shapes
appreciate the use of shapes in forming patterns in fabrics

skills.name: Identify different shapes in the environment
skills.mastery: The child names triangles, squares, rectangles, circles and ovals in objects and pictures (a window, a clock, an egg), in any position, and says the kind of lines each has (straight or curved).
question_forms: name the shape of the object

skills.name: Draw shapes in different ways
skills.mastery: The child draws a triangle, a square, a circle and an oval, freehand and with a ruler or round objects, with the right number of sides.
skills.hands_on: Drawing shapes on manila paper is done in class.

skills.name: Draw and continue patterns involving different shapes
skills.mastery: The child finds the part of a shape pattern that repeats (circle, triangle, triangle), says or draws what comes next, and makes a pattern of their own.

misconceptions.error: Thinks a turned square or triangle is a different shape.

example.question: A square turned on its corner: is it still a square?

misconceptions.reveals: The answer no as a wrong option, with a reason that names the idea.
misconceptions.help: Turn a cut-out and count its equal sides.
misconceptions.source: widely reported in maths-education research; how often Kenyan learners make it is to be confirmed by a teacher

misconceptions.error: Calls an oval a circle.

example.question: An egg is what shape?

misconceptions.reveals: The answer circle as a wrong option, with a reason that names the idea.
misconceptions.help: A circle is the same width every way; an oval is longer one way.

misconceptions.error: Calls a rectangle a square.

example.question: A door is what shape?

misconceptions.cause: Calls every four-sided shape a square.
misconceptions.reveals: The answer square as a wrong option, with a reason that names the idea.
misconceptions.help: A square has all sides equal.

misconceptions.error: Names the object instead of the shape.

example.question: What shape is a clock face?

misconceptions.reveals: The answer clock as a wrong option, with a reason that names the idea.
misconceptions.help: Ask 'what shape?'

misconceptions.error: Leaves gaps at the corners so the shape is not closed.

example.question: Draw a triangle. Do the lines meet?

misconceptions.reveals: The answer gaps at corners as a wrong option, with a reason that names the idea.
misconceptions.help: Start and end at the same point.

misconceptions.error: Draws the wrong number of sides.

example.question: Draw a square. How many sides?

misconceptions.reveals: The answer 3 or 5 as a wrong option, with a reason that names the idea.
misconceptions.help: Count each side as you draw.

misconceptions.error: Draws curved sides on a square or triangle.

example.question: Draw a triangle with a ruler. Are the sides straight?

misconceptions.reveals: The answer curved as a wrong option, with a reason that names the idea.
misconceptions.help: Use a ruler for straight sides.

misconceptions.error: Draws an oval when asked for a circle.

example.question: Draw a circle round a cup. Is it an oval?

misconceptions.reveals: The answer yes as a wrong option, with a reason that names the idea.
misconceptions.help: Trace round a round object.

misconceptions.error: Repeats only the last shape instead of the repeating part.

example.question: circle, triangle, triangle, circle, triangle, triangle, circle, __

misconceptions.cause: Does not find the part that repeats.
misconceptions.reveals: The answer circle as a wrong option, with a reason that names the idea.
misconceptions.help: Ring the part that repeats.

misconceptions.error: Assumes every pattern goes A, B, A, B.

example.question: square, square, circle, square, square, __

misconceptions.cause: Uses a two-step pattern for all.
misconceptions.reveals: The answer square as a wrong option, with a reason that names the idea.
misconceptions.help: Count how many of each in the repeat.

misconceptions.error: Follows the colour and ignores the shape.

example.question: red circle, blue square, red circle, blue __

misconceptions.reveals: The answer circle as a wrong option, with a reason that names the idea.
misconceptions.help: Say the shape name aloud for each.

misconceptions.error: Fills a gap in the middle with the next shape after the gap.

example.question: triangle, circle, __, circle, triangle, circle

misconceptions.reveals: The answer circle as a wrong option, with a reason that names the idea.
misconceptions.help: Say the pattern aloud from the start.
